LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.abs_entropy_sub_l: Let d = TV(p,q) for two laws on an alphabet of size m. For m ≥ 2, |H(p) − H(q)| ≤ h(d) + d ln(m−1), where h is binary entropy in nats. For m = 1, both laws coincide and both sides are zero.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.entropyContinuity: The continuity bound B(m,ε) is zero for m ≤ 1. For m > 1 it is h(ε) + ε ln(m−1) when ε ≤ 1 − 1/m and ln m above that threshold. On [0,1], h is binary entropy in nats. For ε < 0 the definition uses the real extension h(ε) = −ε ln |ε| − (1−ε) ln(1−ε). Continuity estimates use ε ≥ 0.
For fixed alphabet size m, the entropy continuity bound B(m,ε) is nondecreasing in ε on [0,∞).
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.abs_entropy_sub_l: For laws p and q on an m-point alphabet, if TV(p,q) ≤ ε then |H(p) − H(q)| ≤ B(m,ε), the entropy continuity bound at tolerance ε.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.abs_condEntropy_s: Let p and q be joint laws with TV(p,q) ≤ ε, on two alphabets of sizes m and k. Their conditional entropies of the first coordinate given the second differ by at most B(mk,ε) + B(k,ε) in absolute value, where B is the entropy continuity bound.
LeanInfoTheory.Shannon.abs_mutualInfo_su: Let p and q be joint laws with TV(p,q) ≤ ε, on two alphabets of sizes m and k. Their mutual informations differ by at most B(m,ε) + B(k,ε) + B(mk,ε) in absolute value, where B is the entropy continuity bound.
